_note: A ceiling, not a target. Every number below was COUNTED by the counters in tests/guardrails/motion-parity.test.ts, on the integrated motion/p4-token-foundation branch: the token layer plus the three wrappers plus the byte-identical migrations that landed with them (a 0.4/0.86 sheet spring onto Settle; the web's press and calendar-paging curves onto var(--tday-ease-gesture), which is the same (0.2,0.8,0.2,1) they spelled out). They are NOT reproducible at 4c941b1c, which predates the wrappers: counted there, ios.spring is 110 and web.rawCubicBezier is 11, and three of the paths this file excludes do not exist yet. The branch is the unit these numbers belong to, not the commit. The assertion is actual <= budget: this file does not ask anyone to migrate, it asks that nobody add. Lower a number whenever a migration PR takes sites off it; raise one only alongside a call-site comment arguing why that value is deliberately not a token, the way MotionTokens.kt requires.
_measuredBy: tday-web/tests/guardrails/motion-parity.test.ts — the COUNTERS table. The regexes live there rather than here because a count is only meaningful as the output of a rule, and a fixture cannot hold the rule.

_excluded._why: Each path below is a file whose entire job is to hold these numbers once. Counting them would raise every budget by the size of the token layer on the day it landed, and every later migration would move a literal from a counted file to an excluded one for no net change — a ratchet that measures nothing. What is counted is what has NOT been migrated yet.
_excluded.comments: Comment text is stripped before counting, in every language. This PR's own call-site comments argue in place for why a value is NOT a token and quote the numbers while doing it — one of them contains a literal 'response: 0.28,' inside a doc comment. Counting those would let an argument for leaving a value alone raise the budget it is arguing about.
_excluded.notCountedOnPurpose: The ~159 bare Tailwind transition-* utilities in tday-web/src. They ride --default-transition-duration, which is an un-overridden 150ms and therefore already exactly the Quick rung. They are on the vocabulary for free; rebinding that default would be a visible change to all of them.

android._tween: durationMillis = <n>, or tween(<n>. 35 when the token layer landed; one came off in Phase 6 when the root dock's tab tint stopped crossfading on a hand-written 180 and joined the create button and the feed body under them on the Quick rung, and five more when the staged check-off moved onto the rungs — the three rows' fades onto Change, the Completed screen's title colour onto Emphasis when it stopped being the one Android row still on 180/180, plus one 320 that was computed every frame and drawn by nobody. Eight more in Phase 9's 8k, where the other three task feeds joined the one that was already on `TdayFeedItemMotion`. Four were byte-identical to the object and cost nothing to retire: the Completed rows' 190/320/150 triplet and the month header's lone 320, that header having already reached the object's "a displaced item takes Placement and nothing else" rule by hand. The other four are a real ten milliseconds each — the calendar day list's 180/140 and the scheduled home's two file-private `ScheduledTaskHomeItem*` tweens at the same 180/140 — and that is the point: 180 and 140 name no rung, were shared with nothing, and left two of the four task feeds a frame and a half off the other two, which is precisely the drift the object exists to stop. The scheduled home's placement spring stays where it is; Compose's `StiffnessMediumLow` is a library default this counter deliberately does not charge for, and retiming it is a decision about that feed rather than a literal to retire. Five more in Phase 9's 8l, all of them in `TodoListScreen`. Three are the timeline drop placeholder's own `animateItem` triplet, 150/260/120 — the site `docs/motion.md`'s Change bullet names by hand as a placement running on 260 and calls "a call site to settle rather than a reason to widen the rung". A placeholder is an item in the feed: it arrives, the rows under it move down, and it leaves, so it is on `TdayFeedItemMotion` now like everything else in that feed. Two of its three legs retime where anyone can see it — 150 to 190 in, 120 to 150 out — and the third does not: nothing displaces the placeholder while it is up, the dragged row staying in the list and only being styled, and the rows below it gliding on their own `Placement`, so its 260 governed nothing and its 320 governs nothing either. It takes the object's third spec wholesale regardless, because adopting two legs of three is exactly how a site drifts back off — the next hand here should read a triplet, not a pair and a leftover. The other two are the sizes either side of it: the section header's animated bottom spacing on 240 and the placeholder box's own height on 180, both `Durations.Emphasis` now, which is the rung a size change answers to; each keeps `FastOutSlowInEasing` as its argument, the easing never having been the thing in dispute. What 8l did NOT retire is the same file's search-result flash, 420 up and 620 down: those two now carry the call-site argument the fourth idiom rule asks for, and because comment text is stripped before counting, the ceiling goes on paying for them — which is the design, not a leak. Six more in Phase 9's 31a, and they are the last raw tweens in `TdayApp.kt`: the splash and the two legacy auth entry points each wrote `fadeIn(tween(300))` / `fadeOut(tween(300))` of their own over the NavHost's defaults. A route that names its own hand-over is a route that drifts off the rung, and 300 was a third number in a hand-over that should only ever have had one; all three inherit the defaults now. The two `NAV_FADE_*_DURATION_MS` constants those defaults ran on — 360 in and 240 out — went out in the same change onto `Durations.Enter`, and are named here because they are NOT part of the six: a named constant never matched this counter, which is the honest limit of a grep for literals and the reason the row was worth naming in `docs/motion.md`'s non-tokens table rather than left to the ceiling to catch.
android._spring: dampingRatio = <n> or stiffness = <n>, written out. Compose's Spring.StiffnessMediumLow and friends are library defaults rather than decisions — the audit found Android's 400 to be exactly that — so they are not counted and moving onto one is not progress.
android._pressScale: a scale literal in [0.90, 1.0) on a line that also says scale or press. This catches a few enter-scales alongside the press ones (EnterStartScale = 0.92f); they are the same family and the same PRs will touch them, so the over-count is honest rather than convenient. 31 when the ratchet landed, and unmoved until Phase 9's 9b2: the two hero circle buttons — the root feed's search/close pair and the list header's back chevron — each computed a 0.93 of their own from a bare `if (pressed)` inside `graphicsLayer`, so the squash arrived in one frame and left in one under a ripple that took its own time. Both are on `Modifier.tdayPressable` at `PressScales.Bar` now, which is a retune as well as a migration: 0.94, because these are bar buttons and the FAB keeps 0.93. Six more came off in 9b3 and one went back on. The scheduled feed's entire parallel FAB went out with the `showCreateTaskButton` flag — a Scaffold slot, its own private `CreateTaskButton`, and a `PressableIconButton` beside it with no caller anywhere in the tree — and those were two of the 0.93s; the one screen that still drew from that slot, the locked onboarding backdrop, was given a plain `RootCreateTaskButton` instead, so the corner keeps its button and the press behind it is the token one; the today card and the list rows under it stopped inventing 0.97 and 0.98 and named `Card` and `Row`; and the root dock's selector and tab content did the same, the selector's 0.985 being `Row` to the byte. The one that went back on is `TdayPress.FabScale`, which is that same 0.93 written once for the two Android FABs that were each spelling it out. It is a literal in a counted file on purpose: the alternative is a fourth generated token in all three clients, and web's FAB is 0.95. Eight more in 9b1, the leaf-screen sweep: the round bar button that Guide, Calendar, Completed, Latest release and Settings had each copied for themselves, the calendar's accent "Today" pill beside one of them, the sheet chrome's toolbar action and the members sheet's full-width action row. Seven of the eight wrote 0.93 — a depth nothing on Android ever argued for, against `PressScales.Bar`'s 0.94, which iOS did argue, at `TaskFloatingActionButton.swift:162-166` — so those seven are a retune of a hundredth as well as a migration; the eighth was already 0.97 to the byte and merely stopped spelling `Card` out. Nothing was added back: the sheet action's three-way elevation `when` stays where it is, because `cardElevation` has two states and it needs three, and its 1 dp sink and its `enabled` gate are arguments to the modifier rather than literals of its own. Eight more in 9b4, the feed surfaces, and the migration ends there. `TodoListScreen`'s list FAB (the second of the two 0.93s `TdayPress.FabScale` was written for), its Today header button, its Floater list row, and the two list-settings tiles; the category card; and the segmented slider's selector and segment content. Three of those handed an elevation leg back to `CardDefaults.cardElevation` — an `animateDpAsState` fed into `defaultElevation` AND `pressedElevation` is a way of animating an elevation behind Material's back, and the pair it wants is just the two ends. The two slider scales did NOT move onto the modifier and are the only two here that did not: the selector is not a surface reading its own press but a floating pill whose interaction source belongs to an option below it, and both share a spring with the offset that slides it, which the shared modifier deliberately cannot take. They name the token and keep the spring; the selector's 0.985 was `PressScales.Row` to the byte and the segment content moved a half-hundredth onto it so the label and the pill under it press together. THE CEILING AND THE SURVIVORS ARE NOW THE SAME EIGHT, which is what makes a ninth always new: `TaskSwipeActionButton.kt:49` and `CalendarScreen.kt:2978`, each one factor of a composed transform and argued in place (`docs/motion.md`'s "Deliberate non-tokens" table, :547); `TdaySegmentedSlider.kt:205`, a halo growing INTO view rather than a surface sinking; `TdayEmptyState.kt:380`'s `EnterStartScale`, an enter; `TdayHeroTitleHeader.kt:141`'s `DockedTitleScaleFrom`, a scroll-driven dock; `RootFeedDock.kt:500` and `:501`, the tab's own 0.94→1 expansion multiplied by the press token beside it; and `TdayPressable.kt:82`'s `FabScale`, the one press depth in the tree that is still a literal, on purpose and argued where it is written. None of those eight is a press site inventing a depth, so the next line this counter sees will be — the argument `web.rawCubicBezier` already makes for itself two keys down. Phase 9's 31b added a ninth press-family literal and the counter still reads eight, which is worth recording rather than leaving as a discrepancy: `TdayApp.kt`'s `PREDICTIVE_BACK_MIN_SCALE = 0.90f`, the depth the screen a predictive-back drag has hold of recedes to. This regex wants `[Ss]cale` on the line and a SCREAMING_SNAKE constant spells it `SCALE`, so it escapes the same way the two `NAV_FADE_*_DURATION_MS` constants escaped `android.tween` one unit earlier — the honest limit of a grep for literals, twice over. The ceiling is NOT raised for it: a ceiling raised for a literal the counter cannot see is a number the next measurement contradicts. It is carried where the other invisible ones are — `docs/motion.md`'s "Deliberate non-tokens" table, and a marker comment at the declaration that `route-handover.test.ts` now asserts is still there. So the eight survivors named above are still the whole of what this number counts, and a ninth line matching the regex is still always new.

ios._spring: response: <n> and dampingFraction: <n>, counted separately — so one hand-written .spring() costs two. Nineteen of these pairs were the exact 0.28/0.86 that the Snappy token was re-anchored on; none are left. 108 after the token layer landed; four came off in Phase 7's two feed cuts, where the today block and the calendar's day list each stopped timing their rows against a 0.34/0.9 spring nothing else in the repo shared and joined TdayFeedItemMotion. Two more in Phase 8's 35b: the root dock's collapse/expand swap was spelling out 0.34/0.82, which is the Gesture spring exactly — a control carrying on after a finger has let go — so naming the token cost no pixels and is what put a Reduce Motion gate beside it. Four more in Phase 8's 48, where the swipe cleanup took SwipeRevealHintModifier out: its 0.26/0.78 nudge and 0.38/0.68 return are the same two springs TodoTrailingSwipeActionsModifier.revealHint() writes, and the modifier holding the copy had had no caller since the trailing swipe absorbed the hint. Twenty-two more in Phase 9's 8g, where eleven of those nineteen 0.28/0.86 pairs stopped writing the Snappy spring out longhand and named TdayMotion.snappy instead — the onboarding wizard's four-modifier animation chain and the two flow exits that borrow from it, the Settings and Guide search bars opening and closing, and the forgot-password card's step change. The token reads both numbers out of TdayMotionGenerated, so not one of the eleven retimed by a frame; what they bought is that the busiest spring in the repo now says which rung it is, and a rung its own anchor sites do not name is one nobody can find. SwipeActions keeps its 0.34/0.82 pair: that one is an .interactiveSpring, a different constructor with a different blendDuration, and is 8n's to argue. Sixteen more in Phase 9's 8h, the half of that split the Phase 8 accessibility rewrite of these four files had to hold back: the search bars on Calendar, Completed and ScheduledTaskHome, and TodoListScreen's two — its own list search and the floater task home's. Same pair, same token, same zero pixels, and with them the Snappy spring is not written out longhand anywhere in the tree, so the next hand-typed 0.28/0.86 is a new literal rather than one more of nineteen. What is left in these four files is off-token by damping or by frequency — 0.24/0.9, 0.26/0.9, 0.28/0.9 — and moving any of it onto Snappy would be a retiming with a visual review attached, not a refactor; 8n gives each one its comment.
ios._easeDuration: duration: <n> — .easeInOut(duration:), .easeOut(duration:), .snappy(duration:) and the static lets that hold them. Note this is the grep that CANNOT see the generated file's own durations, which are 'static let quick: TimeInterval = 0.15' with no duration: anywhere on the line, and that it equally cannot see TdayMotion.standard(duration: TdayMotion.Durations.change), which is what a migrated site looks like. 56 when the token layer landed; one came off in Phase 6 when the onboarding backdrop stopped timing its blur with a 0.22 of its own, and twenty-two more when the four screens that stage a check-off put its beats on the rungs, and five more when the feed-item split landed: the 0.22 the timeline's travel ran on, the 0.22 the view model wrapped a remote cache change in, and the Completed screen's 0.24/0.16/0.1 trio, all of which are now TdayFeedItemMotion. One more in Phase 8's 35a repair: the root snackbar's .snappy(duration: 0.3) is TdayMotion.snappy, which is both the token that hand-written spring was approximating and the one .animation in AppRootView that Reduce Motion could not switch off — the literal paid for a gate rather than a retiming. Five more in Phase 9's 8m, the five sites whose number already WAS a rung spelled as a digit: HelpGuideScreen's topic card expands on 0.15 and the onboarding wizard's four auth-loading modifiers run on 0.2, which are Quick and Enter exactly. Each kept its .easeInOut — TdayMotion.swift's own docstring says moving an .easeInOut site onto the Standard curve is a visible change that belongs in a PR admitting it, and this is a renaming, not a retiming — so only the number became a name. Both are sites docs/motion.md cites BY LINE as anchors for their rungs, and a rung whose published anchor spells itself as a digit is a rung nobody can grep for. They leave the count for the same reason TdayMotion.standard(duration: TdayMotion.Durations.change) does above: a migrated site puts no digit after the colon, so this grep stops seeing a site the moment that site names its rung. Phase 9's 42c is the PR that admission was waiting for, and it moves no number here: the Guide's topic card is TdayMotion.standard(duration: TdayMotion.Durations.emphasis) now — the retiming and the curve change this counter had already stopped being able to see, which is the honest limit of a grep that measures adoption rather than motion.

web._durationUtility: Tailwind duration-<n> utilities. Most are duration-200, which is already the Enter rung numerically — they are counted anyway, because a utility that happens to equal a token is not the same thing as a site that names one. 73 when the token layer landed; three came off in Phase 6 when the hero header's two sibling controls moved onto duration-quick and its title stopped declaring a transition the rAF was overwriting, and twelve more when the five rows that play the check-off put the strike's colour transition on duration-emphasis and the checkbox's pop on duration-quick. Eleven more in Phase 9's 41a, where web's four overlay systems stopped each timing themselves: the sheet's 500-in/300-out became Emphasis-in/Enter-out (a side panel travelling its own width is geometry, and an exit is never longer than the enter it undoes), and the three centred systems stopped timing themselves too: Modal and the centred selector spell Enter in and Quick out instead of 200/200 and 300/200, while the dialog's one bare duration-200 — the only rung it declares, covering both directions — became one bare duration-enter. Modal's MODAL_EXIT_MS moved with its own class in the same edit: that constant is read twice on purpose, so a rung named on only one side would half-play the exit. Twenty-eight more in Phase 9's 8i, which empties src/components/ of them: twenty-three are duration-200 spelled duration-enter, byte-identical and deliberately so — 200 already IS the Enter rung, so naming it moves no pixel and the only thing that changes is that a reviewer can now see which sites were chosen and which were merely typed. Three named no rung at all. Two of them are rule 2: the install banner rises from off-screen, and the dock's indicator pill both travels and resizes — geometry twice over, Emphasis both. The third, MobileSearchHeader's bar, is on Enter by the ladder's default clause and not by rule 2, because measured in Chromium it times nothing on the toggle it sits on: justify-content is discrete, the bar's children redistribute in one frame, and a parent cannot animate where its children land. The 300 it replaced timed exactly as much; what the declaration still covers is the bar's own background. Two duration-200 moved rather than being renamed. The dock TAB joins the pill on Emphasis because the tab LOSING selection collapses sm:min-w-[104px] → sm:min-w-12 and slides the rest of the row with it — the pill's journey seen from the other end. The arriving tab's own width is content-driven and lands in one frame at any duration, which is why 8i's repair also stopped the pill sampling that rect on a timer and made it follow the rect instead. That retiming carries the tab's hover tint and press squash to Emphasis too, since one duration covers every property the press layer enumerates; it is argued at the call site and has a device row. And the banner's exit drops to Quick, because an offer being declined is the definition of something leaving that nobody is meant to watch go. BANNER_EXIT_MS became DURATION_MS.quick in the same edit for MODAL_EXIT_MS's reason exactly — it is the other half of that one exit and a rung named on one side only half-plays it. Nineteen more in Phase 9's 8j, which empties src/features/ and src/pages/ and takes this counter to ZERO — the one number here that is a floor as well as a ceiling. Eighteen of the nineteen are the same renaming 8i did: fourteen duration-200 spelled duration-enter, byte-identical, across the calendar, the two native dashboards, the Completed tab strip, the list header's edit button and the summary button; plus BlogsPage's four 300s, which named no rung and are duration-change, because nothing on that page changes position or size and a hover reveal is the reader's own pointer played back in place. The nineteenth is the only retiming: the calendar's view-slider thumb ran on 300 while the grid it switches ran on Emphasis, and one tap starts BOTH — changeView sets slideDirection and bumps animKey in the same call — so the control and the view it picked stopped 20ms apart every time; it is duration-emphasis now, which is also rule 2's answer for a thumb that travels, and calendar-pager-height.test.tsx asserts that rung on the thumb beside the one it already asserts on the slide - a counter at zero forbids a number but cannot tell one rung name from another, so the only retiming in the group would otherwise be pinned by nothing. Two sites that travel were deliberately NOT promoted: the Completed tab thumb and the two SettingsPage thumbs are one control shape sitting on Enter, and retiming a control shape is a visible change that has to be argued on its own rather than smuggled in with a rename. Argued at the call site. A zero here means something no other counter in this file means yet: tday-web/src contains no duration-<n> at all outside comment prose, so the next one written anywhere in the web tree is new by construction and turns this red with no arithmetic required.
web._rawCubicBezier: cubic-bezier( written out at a call site. All three survivors are deliberate orphans with no token and no second site: globals.css (0.3,0,0.4,1), RootDock.tsx (0.25,1,0.5,1), AnimatedHeight.tsx (0.22,0.61,0.36,1), the wizard's own height curve promoted with the primitive that now holds it. Cited by curve and not by line: a line number recorded in a fixture is stale the moment anything above it moves, and one of these three moved twice while this PR was being written. With the Gesture curve named, those three orphans ARE the count — the ceiling and the list are the same three sites, so a fourth is always new.
web._cssMsLiteral: a bare <n>ms in CSS or in an inline style string. 19 when the token layer landed; two came off in Phase 5, one of them the inline `height 280ms` the onboarding wizard animated with, which moved to the Emphasis rung when `AnimatedHeight` became a primitive; four more in Phase 6 — `.task-strike`'s own 320ms, and the three `opacity 300ms ease` strings the rows that were not on `taskCompletionTiming` each wrote out for themselves. Two more in Phase 7, when the calendar's two paging slides stopped running on a hand-written 260 and joined the height box under them on Emphasis — the rung both halves of a page turn answer to, the slide moving the grid and the box resizing the card around it. One more when the calendar row's highlight ring joined the tint beside it on the Quick rung. Five more in Phase 7's swipe unit, which is the retiming that note was waiting for: the three rows' `transform 220ms ease` and the two surviving `background-color 150ms ease` beside them are one string in `swipeGesture.ts` now, and a released row settles on Quick going home and Emphasis going open — the rungs the calendar's own pager already answers a refused swipe and a turned page with. Two more in Phase 7's press-cascade unit, which had to name both numbers to argue about them: the blanket press rule's 180 is Quick now — the rung for the app answering a finger, and the un-overridden 150 every bare `transition-*` already rides, so a shadcn Button and a plain one no longer press at two different lengths — and the ripple's 340 is Emphasis, which is the rung a change of size answers to and is that band's own value to within a frame. One more in Phase 7's route hand-over, where the fade a screen arrives on stopped being a hand-written 140 and became `Enter` — the rung for a thing arriving that has no reason to be another length. The 140 was an argument against the LONG end (not `Scene`, not Android's 360) and that half of it is restated at the call site; what it could not defend was 140 itself, which named no rung. The ceiling holds at 2 through Phase 8's reduced-motion floor, which retired one literal to pay for the one it added: `.tday-empty-enter`'s hand-written 520 is `var(--tday-duration-scene)` now — the Scene rung's own and only site, which had simply never been migrated — and the 1ms the blanket floor pins every animation to took its place. That 1ms is the one value here that argues for itself rather than for a rung: zero is what the eye wants, and a zero-length animation's `animationend` is not something every engine agrees to fire, which is the whole reason the floor floors instead of switching motion off.
